task.description: WF-02 Step 3: write test/specs/REQ-042.md and test code under test/letflow/definitions/ for Letflow.Definitions.search/2. Scope test: real executable surface -- continue to full procedure, do not skip.
acceptance_criteria: search/1 with query "invoice" returns a definition named exactly "invoice" ranked above one named "invoice-approval" (partial name match), which in turn ranks above one matched only via its description containing "invoice" -- has a runnable test
search/1 with an empty query string returns a QueryEmpty-equivalent error, not an empty result list -- has a runnable test
search/1 with a query longer than 512 characters returns a QueryTooLong-equivalent error -- has a runnable test
search/1 against a query with no matching name or description anywhere returns an empty list, not an error -- has a runnable test
search/1 respects limit (default 20) and offset for pagination, demonstrated with more matching rows than fit in one page across two successive calls -- has a runnable test

the moduledoc states no new migration/table was added, explicitly citing definition.md's PD-10 section for that boundary -- verify by reading the moduledoc directly, not necessarily an ExUnit assertion
test fixtures use per-test unique data, no cross-test pollution
tests are self-sufficient, no dependency on execution order

result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-042.md and test/letflow/definitions/search_test.exs (DB-backed, real Postgres per DIRECTIVE T-1, provisioned_tenant/1 fixture pattern mirrored from store_test.exs), covering all 6 REQ-042 acceptance criteria: AC1 -- ranking order (exact name match rank 3.0 ranks above partial name match rank 2.0 ranks above description-only match rank 1.0, both rank values and returned-list order asserted); AC2 -- empty query returns {:error, :query_empty}, distinct from an empty list; AC3 -- a 513-byte query returns {:error, :query_too_long} (asserted distinct from :query_empty), plus a 512-byte boundary case proving the '> 512, not >= 512' comparison; AC4 -- a query matching nothing returns {:ok, []}, not an error; AC5 -- limit/offset pagination, two test cases (25 rows across the default 20-row limit + offset:20; 15 rows across an explicit limit:10/offset:0 then limit:10/offset:10), each asserting the two successive pages are disjoint and their union covers every matching row exactly once. AC6 (moduledoc states no new migration/table, citing PD-10) got a 3-test doc-content addition to test/letflow/definitions_test.exs, mirroring that file's existing normalized_moduledoc/1 pattern for REQ-030/REQ-041, plus direct confirmation by reading lib/letflow/definitions.ex's moduledoc text (quoted verbatim in the spec doc). All fixtures use per-test unique tenant schemas (real CREATE SCHEMA + TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1) and System.unique_integer/1-suffixed names/tokens or fresh Ecto.UUID.generate() values; no test depends on another test's data or execution order; no hardcoded secrets/connection strings. 23 tests added/changed across the two files, 0 failures (MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/definitions/search_test.exs test/letflow/definitions_test.exs: '23 tests, 0 failures'). Full project suite re-run after the change: 'mix test' -> '4 properties, 608 tests, 0 failures' (the Keycloak metadata-load error lines in the output are pre-existing placeholder-OIDC-issuer noise, unrelated to this change). mix format --check-formatted passes on both files. Found and filed docs/issues/ISS-0038.yaml (GitHub issue #120) while writing AC1's test: Letflow.Definitions.search/2's @type search_result declares rank: float(), but the shipped CASE-expression fragment returns a %Decimal{} at runtime (confirmed directly -- assert rank_by_id[exact.id] == 3.0 failed with left: Decimal.new("3.0"), right: 3.0 before the fix). Not blocking AC1's own ranking-order behavior (the three tiers still order 3.0 > 2.0 > 1.0 numerically either way), so filed as an adjacent, non-blocking finding per the ISSUE_QUEUE protocol rather than reworked in this run; search_test.exs normalizes via Decimal.to_float/1 with an inline comment pointing at the filed issue.
